# AI Search Readiness (GEO) — eeatminds.in

## llms.txt — present, but Wix-default

`https://www.eeatminds.in/llms.txt` returns **200** (3,354 bytes). Most sites have
none, so this is ahead of the field.

**However, it is auto-generated by Wix, not authored.** Structure:

```
# Eeat Minds
> [one-paragraph business summary]

## Homepage link
- [home](https://www.eeatminds.in/)      ← the ONLY page listed

## AI Agent Access
[Wix MCP endpoint + 7 tool definitions]
```

**The problem:** it links exactly one URL — the homepage. An LLM reading this file
learns the business exists but is pointed at none of the 17 service pages or 68
articles. Roughly 80% of the file is boilerplate documentation of Wix's MCP tools
rather than content about EEAT Minds.

*Severity: Medium. Fix: author a real `llms.txt` listing the money pages and best
articles with one-line descriptions each. This is the highest-leverage GEO action
available and it is a single file.*

Note the summary text does correctly surface the healthcare and real-estate
verticals, which the site's own internal linking largely does not.

## Wix Site MCP endpoint — an unusual asset

`llms.txt` advertises `https://www.eeatminds.in/_api/mcp`, a Model Context Protocol
endpoint exposing `GetBusinessDetails`, `SearchInSite`, `CallWixSiteAPI` and more.
AI agents can query live site content directly rather than scraping.

This is a genuine differentiator most competitors do not have — and it arrived
free with the Wix platform. Worth knowing it exists; worth mentioning in
positioning, since the site sells AI-era SEO.

**Caveat:** `robots.txt` contains `Disallow: /_api/*` for all user agents. The MCP
endpoint lives under `/_api/`, so crawlers are told to avoid the path that
`llms.txt` advertises. Agents calling the endpoint directly are unaffected, but
the two files disagree. Worth reconciling.

## AI crawler access

`robots.txt` contains **no directives for any AI crawler** — no GPTBot, ClaudeBot,
PerplexityBot, CCBot, Google-Extended, Bytespider or Applebot-Extended.

Under the blanket `User-agent: *  Allow: /`, **all AI crawlers are permitted**.
For a business selling AI-search visibility that is the correct posture — but it
is currently an accident of defaults rather than a decision.

*Recommendation: make it explicit. Naming the AI crawlers you allow is also a
demonstrable talking point for clients asking about AI visibility.*

## Citability

Structural factors that determine whether an LLM can quote a page:

| Factor | Status |
|---|---|
| Clean HTML with semantic headings | ✅ single H1 on 83/85 pages |
| FAQ blocks in content | ✅ present on homepage and key pages |
| `FAQPage` schema | ⚠️ **1 page of 85** |
| Author attribution | ❌ **none visible on 68 posts** |
| Publication / update dates | ❌ **none visible** |
| Verifiable external citations | ⚠️ Google Partner link only |
| Named entity with `sameAs` | ✅ strong — 7 profiles on the Person entity |

**The two ❌ rows are the binding constraint.** Assistants preferentially cite
content with a named author and a date, because both are freshness and
accountability signals. 68 undated, unattributed articles are structurally
disadvantaged in AI answers regardless of quality.

This is the same gap flagged in `content.md`, and it costs twice — once in
classic E-E-A-T, once in AI citability.

## Brand entity signals

`sameAs` on the organisation: Facebook, YouTube, Instagram.
`sameAs` on the person: LinkedIn, Instagram, digitalsvp.com, rnsit.ac.in author
page, naveentile.com author page, rnsfgc.edu.in author page, featured.com profile.

Two `.edu.in` author profiles and a `featured.com` expert profile are strong
third-party entity corroboration. The knowledge-graph foundation here is good.

## Priority for this category

1. **Author a real `llms.txt`** listing service pages and key articles (single file)
2. **Add visible bylines + dates to all 68 posts** (also fixes E-E-A-T)
3. **Extend `FAQPage` schema** beyond the single page that has it
4. **Declare AI-crawler policy explicitly** in robots.txt
5. Reconcile `Disallow: /_api/*` against the advertised MCP endpoint
